violations.description: OSCE scenarios lack systematic radiology interpretation frameworks. Clinical images listed generically (e.g., 'ECG', 'CXR', 'Ultrasound') without specifying WHAT to interpret systematically (ABCDE for CXR, 7-step for ECG, ABC for CT)
violations.recommendation: Each OSCE with imaging should specify systematic approach: 'Interpret ECG using 7-step method', 'Interpret CXR using ABCDE approach', 'Interpret CT head using ABC method'

violations.description: Clinical image descriptions are vague placeholders ('for assessment'). OSCEs like CARD-OSCE-0012 (Bradycardia) should specify ECG findings (e.g., '2nd degree heart block Mobitz II') to guide interpretation
violations.recommendation: Replace placeholder descriptions with specific imaging findings (e.g., 'ECG showing complete heart block with dissociated P waves and QRS', 'CXR showing right middle lobe consolidation with air bronchograms')

violations.description: Mixed terminology consistency issues. Some OSCEs use correct Australian terms ('Gastro-esophageal Reflux' GENE-OSCE-0020) but others lack radiology-specific Australian terminology guidance (e.g., 'oedema' not 'edema', 'theatre' not 'OR')
violations.location: Multiple OSCEs - terminology not standardized across imaging content
violations.recommendation: Add Australian radiology terminology standard to each imaging OSCE: 'Use Australian terms: pulmonary oedema, theatre, paracetamol, adrenaline'

violations.description: No technical adequacy assessment requirements. CXR OSCEs (CARD-OSCE-0018 Pulmonary Edema, GENE-OSCE-0027 Post-op SOB, GENE-OSCE-0028 Lung Cancer) should require rotation/inspiration/penetration checks before interpretation
violations.location: CXR-based OSCEs (9 total) - no technical quality assessment specified
violations.recommendation: Add to CXR OSCEs: 'Assess technical adequacy (RIPI: Rotation, Inspiration, Penetration, Inclusion) before systematic ABCDE interpretation'

violations.description: ECG OSCEs (11 total: CARD-OSCE-0009/0012/0013/0019, GAST-OSCE-0041/0042) lack 7-step systematic method specification. Should mandate: Rate → Rhythm → Axis → Intervals → P waves → QRS → ST/T
violations.location: ECG-based OSCEs across cardiology and gastroenterology
violations.recommendation: Add to all ECG OSCEs: 'Use 7-step systematic ECG interpretation: 1. Rate, 2. Rhythm, 3. Axis, 4. Intervals (PR/QRS/QT), 5. P waves, 6. QRS complex, 7. ST segments & T waves'

violations.description: Missing critical findings identification requirements. OSCEs like CARD-OSCE-0013 (Long QT) should specify red flags (Torsades risk), CARD-OSCE-0016 (Cardiac Syncope) should require exclusion of life-threatening arrhythmias
violations.location: High-risk imaging OSCEs (STEMI, stroke, trauma) - no critical findings mandate
violations.recommendation: Add 'Critical Findings Checklist' to high-risk OSCEs: List must-identify findings (e.g., STEMI → ST elevation ≥2mm V2-V4, reciprocal ST depression, territory identification)

violations.description: CT imaging OSCEs (GENE-OSCE-0028 Lung Cancer CT Chest, GAST-OSCE-0035 Liver Disease, GAST-OSCE-0036 Pancreatitis CT Abdomen) lack ABC systematic approach (Asymmetry, Blood, CSF spaces for head; Airway/Bones/Circulation for chest/abdomen)
violations.recommendation: Specify CT systematic approach: 'CT Head: ABC (Asymmetry/midline shift, Blood/hemorrhage, CSF spaces/ventricles)', 'CT Chest: Mediastinum → Lungs → Pleura → Bones', 'CT Abdomen: Solid organs → Bowel → Vessels → Free fluid'

violations.description: Ultrasound OSCEs (CARD-OSCE-0017 Upper Limb DVT, ENDO-OSCE-0006 Thyroid Ultrasound) lack Australian ultrasound reporting standards (ASUM guidelines, Doppler terminology)
violations.recommendation: Add Australian ultrasound standards: 'Use ASUM reporting format: Indication, Technique, Findings, Impression. Doppler: spectral waveform analysis, colour flow mapping'

violations.description: No mention of comparison to prior imaging. Best practice radiology requires stating if comparison films available (e.g., 'Compared to CXR 6 months ago, new right lower lobe consolidation')
violations.location: All imaging OSCEs - no prior comparison requirement
violations.recommendation: Add to all imaging OSCEs: 'State if comparison to prior imaging available. If yes, describe interval changes. If no, state 'No prior imaging available for comparison''

violations.description: Missing clinical correlation requirement. Imaging interpretation should always correlate with clinical presentation (e.g., CXR consolidation + fever/cough → community-acquired pneumonia)
violations.location: All imaging OSCEs - clinical correlation not mandated
violations.recommendation: Add to all imaging OSCEs: 'Correlate imaging findings with clinical presentation. State if findings consistent with clinical diagnosis or suggest alternative diagnosis'

manual_review_reasons: CRITICAL DEFICIENCY: All 52 imaging OSCEs lack systematic interpretation framework specification (ABCDE, 7-step ECG, ABC CT). Candidates may interpret randomly without structure.

CRITICAL DEFICIENCY: Generic placeholder clinical image descriptions ('for assessment') provide no guidance on WHAT imaging findings to identify. Real OSCE stations require specific abnormalities (e.g., 'ECG showing ST elevation in II/III/aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I/aVL').
MAJOR DEFICIENCY: No technical adequacy assessment required for CXR OSCEs (9 total). Australian radiology standards mandate checking Rotation/Inspiration/Penetration/Inclusion BEFORE interpretation.
MAJOR DEFICIENCY: ECG OSCEs (11 total) do not specify 7-step systematic method. Without mandatory structure, candidates may miss critical findings (axis, intervals, ST changes).

DEPLOYMENT RISK: High-stakes imaging OSCEs (STEMI ECG CARD-OSCE-0019, stroke CT NEUR-OSCE-0049, tension pneumothorax) lack 'Critical Findings Checklist'. Missing life-threatening findings = patient safety risk.
QUALITY CONCERN: Mixed Australian terminology consistency. Some OSCEs correct ('gastro-oesophageal'), but no radiology-specific terminology standard enforced across all imaging content.

Content generation system likely used generic templates without radiology expert input. Requires radiology-interpretation-expert agent review + re-generation with systematic approach specifications embedded.

URGENT: Replace ALL generic clinical_images descriptions with specific imaging findings (e.g., 'ECG: sinus bradycardia 42 bpm, 2:1 AV block, PR interval 240ms')
HIGH PRIORITY: Add 'Technical Adequacy Assessment' section to all 9 CXR OSCEs (RIPI: Rotation, Inspiration, Penetration, Inclusion)
HIGH PRIORITY: Add 'Critical Findings Checklist' to 15 high-risk imaging OSCEs (STEMI, stroke, trauma, pneumothorax, free air, aortic dissection)
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Embed 7-step ECG systematic approach in all 11 ECG OSCEs (Rate → Rhythm → Axis → Intervals → P → QRS → ST/T)
MEDIUM PRIORITY: Add Australian radiology terminology standard to each OSCE header (oedema, theatre, paracetamol, adrenaline, RANZCR reporting format)
LOW PRIORITY: Add prior imaging comparison requirement + clinical correlation statement to all imaging OSCEs
VALIDATION: Run pre-flight validation on regenerated OSCEs to confirm systematic approach present in 100% of imaging content

violations.issue: OSCEs provide only topic titles (e.g., 'OSA', 'Hyperthyroidism') without medication management scenarios
violations.suggested_fix: Transform generic topics into medication-focused scenarios. Example for GENE-OSCE-0022 (OSA): 'Patient diagnosed with severe OSA (AHI 42). Current medications: metoprolol 50mg BD, atorvastatin 40mg nocte. Task: Counsel on CPAP therapy, review medications that worsen OSA (benzodiazepines, opioids), adjust timing of metoprolol to avoid nocturnal bradycardia.'

suggestions: For ENDO-OSCE-0001 (Hyperthyroidism): Add scenario like 'Patient with Graves disease, TSH <0.01, fT4 42. Prescribe: carbimazole 15mg TDS (PBS authority required), propranolol 40mg TDS for symptomatic control. Counsel on: agranulocytosis symptoms, need for FBC monitoring, Australian drug name (carbimazole, NOT methimazole).'

For ENDO-OSCE-0003 (DKA): Include insulin protocol (Actrapid 0.1 units/kg/hr IV), potassium replacement (20mmol/L in fluids if K+ 3.5-5.5), fluid resuscitation (normal saline 1L over 1hr), monitoring (VBG q2h, electrolytes q4h).

For CARD-OSCE-0012 (Bradycardia): Specify patient on atenolol 100mg daily for hypertension, HR 42, symptomatic (dizziness). Task: Cease atenolol (renally cleared beta-blocker), switch to amlodipine 5mg daily (no renal adjustment), arrange cardiology review for possible pacemaker.

For GENE-OSCE-0024 (Iron Deficiency Anemia): Prescribe ferrous sulfate 325mg (105mg elemental iron) daily on empty stomach, counsel on: take with vitamin C (enhances absorption), avoid with tea/coffee (tannins reduce absorption), PBS-listed, common side effects (constipation, black stools).

For GAST-OSCE-0039 (Hyponatremia): Include medication review for SIADH-inducing drugs (SSRIs, carbamazepine, PPIs), fluid restriction (800-1000mL/day), cease thiazide diuretic if drug-induced, monitor sodium q12h (avoid rapid correction >10mmol/24hr to prevent osmotic demyelination).

For all OSCEs: Add 'Medications' section with: current_medications (list with doses/frequencies), new_prescriptions_required (Australian names, PBS codes), drug_interactions_to_assess, counseling_points, monitoring_requirements

The file contains OSCE skeleton structures (metadata, topic titles, generic scenarios) but lacks the essential medication details required for pharmacological assessment: no drug names (Australian or otherwise), no doses, no frequencies, no routes, no PBS codes, no drug interactions, no prescribing tasks, no medication reconciliation content. This is analogous to being asked to evaluate a recipe when only the dish name is provided. The 52 OSCEs must be populated with detailed medication management scenarios before medication-management-expert evaluation can proceed. Score of 4.0 acknowledges the structural foundation is present (hence not 0.0), but content is insufficient for specialty evaluation. All criteria_scores marked 0.0 indicate 'not applicable/unable to assess' rather than 'assessed and failed'. Recommendation: Route to clinical-documentation-expert or content-generation agent FIRST to populate medication details, THEN return to medication-management-expert for Australian medication standards validation.
